nodes.label: CLAUDE.md project instructions and house rules
Parser rule 1: a bad value costs its field, a missing hook throws
nodes.rationale: A ParseError escaping a row loop discards every other item on the page. If the element or attribute is gone the page shape changed: throw. If the hook is there and the value is unreadable: record it in extra.unparsed*, warn, keep the row. Found 3×.

nodes.label: Parser rule 2: silent empty is the worst outcome
nodes.rationale: If a container exists and its rows stopped matching, that is a redesign, not an empty page — throw. Guarding the container alone is not enough; guard the rows too. Found 2×.

nodes.label: Parser rule 3: never index cells positionally
nodes.rationale: Anchor on a data-testid, a class, or the table's own header row. cells[2] turns one added column into a page of undated, mis-statused items with no error. Found 1×, cost 14 items.

nodes.label: Parser rule 4: guard duplicate sourceIds on one page
nodes.rationale: §3's raw map is keyed by memberKey, so a collision silently merges two items into one. Found 3×.

nodes.label: Parser rule 5: typeof x === 'string' is not validation
nodes.rationale: '' passes it and shadows the fallback; Date.parse accepts naive times and bare dates (a bare 2026-09-11 lands at 7pm the previous day); Number('') is 0. Validate the shape positively with an anchored regex. Found 4×.

nodes.label: Parser rule 6: match markers exactly and scope them to the smallest element
nodes.rationale: 'not submitted' contains 'submitted'; an exam title containing an empty-state sentence blanked its whole card. Found 2×.

nodes.label: Parser rule 7: RawItem.url is https on the source origin or the fallback
nodes.rationale: Resolving against a base silently accepts //other.host, javascript: and http:, and throws on a malformed href. Found 3×.

nodes.label: Parser rule 8: login detection needs the HTTP status
nodes.rationale: An expired session on an API path returns 401 with JSON at the unchanged URL; without the status that reads as logged in and the parser reports parse_error instead of needs_login, which is §0 rule 2's whole point. Found 2×.

nodes.label: Parser rule 9: the capture beats the spec
nodes.rationale: Where real markup contradicts SPEC.md the capture wins, but the amendment is written down in docs/<source>-findings.md and PROGRESS.md's amendments list with the evidence.

nodes.label: Parser rule 10: a test that passes against a wrong implementation is not a test
nodes.rationale: Before calling a behaviour covered, mutate the source in a scratch copy and confirm the suite fails; where realistic fixture values cannot distinguish, make a fixture row deliberately unrealistic and say so in the README.

nodes.label: Parser rule 11: never signed in is not session expired, and both are needs_login
nodes.rationale: A student who has never signed in gets 200 at the unchanged URL with an ordinary title (Gradescope marketing splash, PrairieTest with no cards), so the parser throws parse_error — offering nothing to click in the one case where signing in is the fix. Every hosted source needs a positive signed-out marker. Found 2× on a real beta build.

nodes.label: Parser rule 12: a signed-out marker must be absent from the healthy page
nodes.rationale: A marker that also matches a signed-in page turns every successful sync into needs_login and freezes the list silently. 'Log In' is not safe (an assignment 'Log Interpretation' contains it); anchor on a class hook or a path, and build a deliberately adversarial fixture.

nodes.label: Parser rule 13: a per-student URL means a source, not an adapter
nodes.rationale: An adapter has one fixed url, so anything addressed by an enrolment or account id (smartPhysics's /Course?enrollmentID=…) cannot be served by one. Check the URL shape before writing selectors; it decides between a JSON entry and a two-stage fetch plan.

nodes.label: Worker rule 1: the service worker is the file the suite cannot reach, so keep it empty
nodes.rationale: Every live defect lived in background.ts because that is the only place a decision was unreachable by a test. Anything with a decision belongs in core/; the worker should be chrome.* calls and wiring. core/queue.ts exists because a deadlock hid in the worker for four steps.

nodes.label: Worker rule 2: a green dot must mean 'I fetched, and it was fine'
nodes.rationale: A source that is off, unconfigured or resting reports that. syncSites returned [] with no adapters enabled and the loop recorded ok; defaultStatus seeded state ok before any request; set-source-enabled painted ok on a mere toggle; the status line read lastSyncAt. Anything the UI asserts about a source must derive from an attempt that happened — pending is a real state, core/health.ts owns the derivation. Classify network vs parse failure before reporting.

nodes.label: Worker rule 3: a value this code invented is not a value the source stated
nodes.rationale: §4.5's runner fills in 23:59 for a bare date; §5.3 ranked that invention above a real Canvas deadline. Mark what was assumed (extra.timeAssumed) and make every precedence rule prefer a stated value. Whenever a default is filled in, ask what downstream code will treat it as authoritative.

nodes.label: Worker rule 4: every store writer goes through the queue, and the queue is re-entrant
nodes.rationale: An unqueued write is read and then overwritten seconds later by a sync holding the queue, with no error and a control that springs back. A non-re-entrant queue deadlocks the moment one queued path calls another (sync → reschedule → fireNotification), permanently.

nodes.label: Worker rule 5: log both branches of any decision the user will have to debug
nodes.rationale: A silent early return in the registry seed made 'already seeded' and 'the seed never ran' identical in the console, costing two rounds of browser time — the most expensive resource in the project.

nodes.label: Worker rule 6: a mutation check proves a test is load-bearing, not that it pins the right requirement
nodes.rationale: The state: ok defect survived a mutation-checked suite because a test asserted it. When a defect turns up in covered code, look for the test pinning the bug; when writing a test from a spec line, quote the line.

nodes.label: Worker rule 7: live data is a source of truth the fixtures are not
nodes.rationale: Four defects came from one real sync; three could not exist in a fixture test because they need two sources, a queue, or a browser. Read live output as evidence rather than confirmation.

nodes.label: Worker rule 8: a message from the worker is data from another build, not a typed object
nodes.rationale: Chrome reloads an extension page from disk on every open but keeps the running service worker, so the two routinely disagree. Response is a compile-time claim about the sender's build; normalize every field a page dereferences (core/compat.ts), name missing ones on screen, never let a render function reject into a console the user does not have open.

nodes.label: Mutation rule 1: verify the mutation applied
nodes.rationale: Twice a sed reported 'survived' when it had never patched anything. A false survived says a behaviour is unpinned when it is pinned, and the natural response is a redundant test or deleting a live guard. Assert the match count first.

nodes.label: Mutation rule 2: a survivor is untested, unreachable, or redundant
nodes.rationale: Untested: write the test. Unreachable: keep it with a comment saying why (collapseOverdue's third-lead clause). Redundant: a second guard rejecting exactly what the first does (isRealWallClock before wallClockToIso) is not defence — delete it.

nodes.label: Mutation rule 3: a survivor sometimes indicts the design
nodes.rationale: cellByHeader and headerExists each wrote out the header-matching rule, so loosening one was masked by the other. The fix was one resolveColumn used by both, not a cleverer test.

nodes.label: When live data contradicts a document: rewrite the claim
nodes.rationale: canvas-findings.md said Canvas cannot contribute any deadlines; a live sync returned one. A 'superseded' note under the sentence leaves the false claim first. Rewrite it, ask whether it was wrong when written, then follow what was inferred from it — G2's Canvas exemption and G1's 'no planner fixture obtainable' were both wrong.

nodes.label: The popup is measured by Chrome, not sized by you
nodes.rationale: body { max-height: 600px; overflow-y: auto } made body its own scroll container, leaving no intrinsic height to measure, so Chrome opened the popup at 800×600. Chrome already caps at 600 and scrolls; the width belongs on html too. Never make body/html a scroll container, be suspicious of viewport units, and never key layout off window width (it feeds itself). The harness has to be the real document.

nodes.label: Check it in the mode Sushi actually uses (dark)
nodes.rationale: Every verification screenshot was light while Sushi's machine is dark. A tint does different work at each end: 5.5% navy on white drops 12/255, 6% pale blue on #1c1c1c lifts 8, and the eye is less sensitive near black — dark tints are roughly double. Measure the composited luminance rather than trusting the alpha.

nodes.label: UI rule 1: a popup and the service worker have different consoles
nodes.rationale: Five rounds were spent on the background.js inspector, which cannot contain a page's errors. Say which console; prefer the full view, an ordinary tab with ordinary devtools.

nodes.label: UI rule 2: every send() from a page needs a .catch
nodes.rationale: Four correction handlers were void send(…).then(…) with no catch, so a rejection became invisible in the UI and the worker console — and send rejects with the one message that explains the commonest cause (the worker runs older code).

nodes.label: UI rule 3: a status line at the bottom of the document is not a channel
nodes.rationale: #status sat below ~1100px of week view in a 600px window; every failure it reported for a month landed below the fold. A report has to be reachable from where the error happened.

nodes.label: UI rule 4: when a control does something asynchronous, say so on the control
nodes.rationale: 'Hide' becoming 'Applying…' distinguishes 'the click never ran' from 'the click ran and the round trip failed' with no console at all; one change produced more information than four builds of logging.

nodes.label: UI rule 5: a synthetic .click() is not a press
nodes.rationale: It fires no pointerdown, mousedown, focus change or default action, so every harness check of the row menu passed while the real menu was unusable.

nodes.label: UI rule 6: the preview pane's coordinates are not the page's
nodes.rationale: Real mouse events aimed at the pane landed in dead space and 'the menu never opens' was nearly reported as a finding. If a click-driven result is surprising, verify the click landed.

nodes.label: UI rule 7: a class selector matches whole tokens
nodes.rationale: Three redraw guards asked for .menu while the class was menu-surface, so all three were dead and any store write or minute tick deleted an open menu. Route a selector and its class through one constant so the wrong answer is unspellable.

nodes.label: UI rule 8: height is the popup's recurring bug in different costumes
nodes.rationale: A menu below the fold, a floating panel contributing no height, a status line out of sight, the sources panel clipped — all the 600px ceiling. When something 'does not work', measure where it is before reading what it does.

nodes.label: HANDOFF 2026-09-13: the row menu receives no mouse events
nodes.rationale: The menu opens but Hide/Mark done/Split/Merge do nothing: a capture-phase probe in openRowMenu shows not even pointerdown reaches the menu element. Ruled out: handler wiring, message routing, swallowed errors, redraws, focusout, below-the-fold, stacking order, pointer-events. Next: check for two .menu-surface elements (the health popover shares the class), whether the menu is still connected, and document.elementFromPoint() under the pointer. Remove the TEMPORARY probe once solved.

nodes.label: Open: course sites split across pages
nodes.rationale: An adapter is one fixed URL and ECE 391 keeps assignments on schedule.html and exams on exams.html, so half of such a course can never be read. Needs a decision — several adapters per course or an adapter with several URLs — not a patch.

nodes.label: Open: Coursera for the online CS courses
nodes.rationale: Blocked on whether a Coursera deadline URL carries an account or enrolment id: per-student means a source (a day's work), a fixed per-course URL means a registry entry and no build (house rule 13).

nodes.label: Chrome Web Store submission (draft, not submitted)
nodes.rationale: Draft mimgaiaicopabbiabakmknkcbfekplei. Listing copy, description and privacy-form answers are written; outstanding in the developer console: re-upload the zip, host-permission justification, tick Website content, test instructions, Unlisted visibility, submit. §9 still gates G5 behind G4.

nodes.label: Review policy
nodes.rationale: Full adversarial review (~20 min, ~1.5M tokens) only for core/dedupe.ts and the sync loop, where G2/G3 risk lives; light or no review for refactors and UI, relying on the mutation-tested suite. Findings whose refuters fail are unverified, not refuted.

nodes.label: Trace the path, not just the file
nodes.rationale: Reviewing background.ts as a file found nothing in four steps; fanning agents over segments of one runtime path (bundle → storage → options → permission → sync → offscreen → popup) found the deadlock, the unqueued writer and the repeating failed fetch in one pass. Findings from a trace are leads, not results; verify each against the code.

nodes.label: Parallelism policy
nodes.rationale: Steps 7–8 stay sequential (one tightly coupled core, one decision-maker). Steps 9–12 ran in parallel and it worked. More coder agents do not fix a recurring defect class; shared helpers and house rules do. Parallelise investigation more readily than implementation.

nodes.label: Sushi's time is the scarce resource
nodes.rationale: Every browser round-trip is a real interruption. Ask for one action at a time with exact steps and what each answer would prove; exhaust what the repo can answer first; prefer diagnostics that distinguish several hypotheses; when a round-trip is spent on something a log line would have answered, add the log line.

nodes.label: Development loop (dist/ as unpacked extension)
nodes.rationale: Load dist/ once from chrome://extensions, then npm run build or watch and click reload on the card; zips are only for testers.
